score.cap: grade limited to F: IPv4 INPUT accepts every new connection

findings.title: INPUT accepts new connections to any port
findings.detail: No rule refuses them, and the policy of filter/INPUT is ACCEPT. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.

fix.summary: Add rules for the traffic that is needed and test them, with a way back, then set the policy to DROP. The recommended baseline (--baseline) is a complete rule set to start from.

findings.title: 5 services are open to any source because INPUT accepts by default
findings.detail: No rule names their ports: sshd on 22/tcp; nginx on 80/tcp (IPv4 only); nginx on 443/tcp (IPv4 only); mysqld on 3306/tcp (IPv4 only); dhclient on 68/udp (IPv4 only). Close the default first; then accept each port that must stay reachable, for its clients only.

findings.title: All ports of the containers on bridge br-982052ef0162 are reachable by direct routing
findings.detail: Every port of containers on bridge br-982052ef0162 (gateway mode nat-unprotected) is forwarded to hosts that route 172.29.0.2 via this host (for example on the same L2 segment), including ports that were never published; neither INPUT nor published-port rules apply.

fix.summary: Use the default gateway mode "nat" for this network, or drop new non-DNAT connections into the bridge in DOCKER-USER.

steps.text: Drop packets for the containers that do not arrive from their bridge (published ports keep working)
Or refuse new connections into the bridge that no published port translated
steps.command: iptables -I DOCKER-USER -o br-982052ef0162 ! -i br-982052ef0162 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m conntrack ! --ctstate DNAT -j DROP

findings.title: 6 Docker published ports are open to any source
findings.detail: Docker translates these ports to containers, and filter/FORWARD accepts them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 8080/tcp to 172.17.0.2:80; IPv4 8082/tcp of 192.168.88.217 to 172.17.0.4:80; IPv4 9053/udp to 172.17.0.5:53; IPv4 9000-9002/tcp to 172.17.0.6:9000-9002; IPv4 8091/tcp to 172.29.0.2:80; IPv4 8443/tcp to 172.30.0.2:443; IPv6 8443/tcp to [fd00:dead:beef::2]:443.

fix.summary: Docker translates published ports in nat/PREROUTING, so they are forwarded and never reach filter/INPUT (this includes INPUT rules of ufw or firewalld). Restrict them in DOCKER-USER, which runs before Docker's own rules and which Docker never flushes. Packets are already translated there: match the published port with --ctorigdstport, not --dport. A service that only local clients need can be published on loopback instead (docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:<container-port>). The commands below are for port 8080/tcp. For each of the other ports (8082/tcp of 192.168.88.217, 9053/udp, 9000-9002/tcp, 8091/tcp, 8443/tcp), run them again with its protocol and its port; write a range of ports as FIRST:LAST. For a port of one address, add --ctorigdst ADDRESS; for a port of all addresses, leave that match out. For IPv6, use ip6tables.

steps.text: Allow the trusted sources of port 8080 first
steps.command: iptables -I DOCKER-USER 1 -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN

steps.text: Then drop the rest of that port
steps.command: iptables -I DOCKER-USER 2 -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP

findings.title: Container port 172.31.0.2:80 is reachable by direct routing
findings.detail: Container port 172.31.0.2:80/tcp on bridge br-84b7b034b576 (gateway mode routed) is forwarded without NAT to hosts that route 172.31.0.2 via this host (for example on the same L2 segment); host INPUT rules do not apply to it.

fix.summary: Restrict the container port in DOCKER-USER (match -d 172.31.0.2 --dport 80), or use gateway mode nat.

steps.text: Drop the container port for all but the trusted sources

findings.title: OUTPUT default policy is ACCEPT
findings.detail: All outbound traffic is allowed. This is the usual setup; an OUTPUT allowlist can limit what a compromised service is able to reach.

baseline.ipv4:
# Recommended IPv4 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (iptables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "iptables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and DOCKER-USER and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p icmp -m icmp --icmp-type 8 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Other listening services found on this host. Uncomment only what must be
# reachable, preferably with -s <trusted-cidr>:
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # nginx
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # nginx
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 3306 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # mysqld
# -A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 68 -j ACCEPT   # dhclient
# Docker: published ports never reach INPUT. Restrict them here; packets are
# already DNATed, so match the published port with conntrack, not --dport.
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.17.0.2:80
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdst 192.168.88.217 --ctorigdstport 8082 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.17.0.4:80
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdst 192.168.88.217 --ctorigdstport 8082 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8091 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.29.0.2:80
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8091 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8443 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.30.0.2:443
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8443 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 9000:9002 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.17.0.6:9000-9002
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 9000:9002 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
# -A DOCKER-USER -p udp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 9053 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> 172.17.0.5:53
# -A DOCKER-USER -p udp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 9053 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN
COMMIT
baseline.ipv6:
# Recommended IPv6 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (ip6tables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "ip6tables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and DOCKER-USER and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Neighbor discovery is untracked by conntrack and must be allowed explicitly;
# a hop limit of 255 proves the sender is on-link.
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 134 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "router advertisement (SLAAC)" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 135 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor solicitation" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 136 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor advertisement" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 130 -m comment --comment "multicast listener query" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -d fe80::/10 -p udp -m udp --sport 547 --dport 546 -m comment --comment "DHCPv6 client" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s ::1/128 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 128 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh6-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Docker: published ports never reach INPUT. Restrict them here; packets are
# already DNATed, so match the published port with conntrack, not --dport.
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8443 --ctdir ORIGINAL -s <trusted-cidr> -j RETURN   # published -> [fd00:dead:beef::2]:443
# -A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8443 --ctdir ORIGINAL -j DROP
-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN
COMMIT
notes: SSH stays reachable on TCP port 22 (detected from the listening sshd).
Both families are always generated: IPv6 gets addresses automatically (SLAAC), so an unused stack must be closed too.

Persist the result with your distribution's mechanism (e.g. iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4 with iptables-persistent).
Docker hosts: always use --noflush. A full restore deletes Docker's chains and disconnects all containers until dockerd restarts.
